videos.script: One class can do two jobs that pull in opposite directions. {{two}} It changes the library: it lends a copy, takes a return, places a reservation, and refuses when a rule says no. And it answers questions for screens: what is on the shelf, who has what, how many people are waiting. {{questions}} The rules want a small model with nothing in it but what they check. The screens want every title already joined to its author and its count. {{pull}} This lesson starts from an old rule of Bertrand Meyer's. A method either changes something or answers a question, never both. {{meyer}} Then it applies the same rule to whole models. Commands go to a write model that enforces the rules. Queries go to a read model shaped for one screen. {{split}} You will build both on the library's copies and reservations, connect them with events, and watch the read model fall behind when its update runs later. {{lag}} And you will see when all of this costs more than it saves, which is more often than its fans admit. {{cost}}
